newsitem.title: USA: Clinton nominates Rohatyn as ambassador to France.
newsitem.headline: Clinton nominates Rohatyn as ambassador to France.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton on Friday announced the nomination of Felix Rohatyn, a prominent New York investment banker, to be U.S. ambassador to France.

The White House announced the nomination, which is subject to the approval of the U.S. Senate, in a statement released in Harrison, Arkansas, where Clinton was attending the funeral of an old friend and political supporter, Hilary Jones.
Rohatyn retired this year as managing director of Lazard Freres & Co., a New York investment bank with French roots that has major related operations in London and Paris.

In addition to his work as an investment banker, Rohatyn has taken an active role in public life, serving as chairman of the Municipal Assistance Corporation for the city of New York. He is also a leading contributor to the Democratic Party.
He was a key player in negotiations that restructured the city's finances during a fiscal crisis in the mid-1970s.

Having worked for Lazard Freres since 1948, Rohatyn is already well known in French official and financial circles. He was awarded the Legion of Honour by the French government in 1983 and was elevated to the rank of commander in 1995.
Clinton had wanted to nominate him as vice chairman of the Federal Reserve Board last year, but backed off from the plan when it became clear the Senate was unlikely to confirm Rohatyn for the post.
He succeeds British-born aristocrat Pamela Harriman as ambassador. Harriman died in February at age 76 after suffering a stroke while swimming at a Paris hotel.
Harriman, a member of a minor English noble family, was Winston Churchill's daughter-in-law for the brief wartime period in which she was married to his son Randolph.
She was also married to millionaire Democratic Party activist W. Averell Harriman and was considered one of America's best-connected women.
